Tackle avoidance dynamics dictate that a pass must be executed only when imminent danger is present, introducing a temporal constraint. Pass accuracy urgency reflects the inverse relationship between execution speed and precision—when urgency rises, accuracy plummets. Defensive convergence vector captures the directional mismatch between offensive and defensive movements, where attackers move toward the ball while defenders move away, creating a strategic imbalance. These three primitives form a triadic system: tackle avoidance sets the temporal boundary, pass urgency defines the accuracy trade-off, and defensive convergence determines the spatial risk landscape. Together they model the dual nature of pass execution—both a tactical necessity and a high-risk maneuver.
